content.value_statement: Random content wastes resources and leaves buyer needs uncovered. This skill turns customer, keyword, and market evidence into focused pillars and priorities.
actual_capabilities: Builds three to five content pillars from business, audience, customer, and competitor context.
Maps topics to awareness, consideration, decision, and implementation stages.
Classifies ideas as searchable, shareable, or both.
Scores ideas using customer impact, content-market fit, search potential, and resource requirements.
Organizes hub-and-spoke topic clusters with internal linking guidance.
Analyzes provided keyword exports, transcripts, surveys, and customer feedback for content opportunities.
limitations: Does not write complete articles and directs individual copywriting tasks to a separate skill.
Does not provide live keyword volumes unless the user supplies data or enables web research.
Recommendations depend on accurate business, audience, and customer research context.
CMS guidance covers strategy, content models, workflows, and high-level platform comparisons.

use_cases.title: Launch a SaaS Blog
use_cases.description: Create initial pillars, buyer-stage topics, and priorities for a new business blog.

use_cases.title: Prioritize a Limited Calendar
use_cases.description: Rank many content ideas against customer value, market fit, search potential, and available resources.

use_cases.title: Build Topical Authority
use_cases.description: Design hub-and-spoke clusters that organize related topics and strengthen internal linking.

prompt_templates.title: Create Basic Pillars
prompt_templates.prompt: Create three content pillars for [company], which serves [audience] and solves [problem]. Explain each pillar and suggest five topics.
prompt_templates.scenario: Start a strategy with basic business and audience context.

prompt_templates.title: Rank Content Ideas
prompt_templates.prompt: Prioritize these ideas for [company]: [ideas]. Score customer impact, content-market fit, search potential, and resources. Explain the ranking.
prompt_templates.scenario: Choose the strongest ideas when time or budget is limited.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Topic Cluster
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a hub-and-spoke cluster for [topic]. Include one hub, twelve spokes, buyer stages, search intent, formats, and internal links.
prompt_templates.scenario: Plan connected coverage for a strategic topic.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Evidence-Based Roadmap
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [keyword data, transcripts, and competitor notes]. Build a quarterly roadmap with weighted scores, content dependencies, measurable goals, and CMS workflow requirements.
prompt_templates.scenario: Combine several research sources into an advanced operating plan.

output_examples.input: Plan content pillars for expense software serving finance teams.
output: Cash flow control: budgeting, forecasting, and policy topics tied to financial oversight.
Expense operations: approvals, reimbursements, cards, and reporting workflows.
Compliance and risk: audit readiness, fraud prevention, and tax documentation.

output_examples.input: Prioritize onboarding, pricing, template, and industry trend topics with limited resources.
output: First: onboarding template, because it offers strong customer value, product alignment, search demand, and manageable effort.
Second: pricing comparison, because it supports decision-stage buyers but needs current competitor research.
Later: industry trend report, because original data requires more resources.

best_practices: Provide business goals, audience details, customer language, existing performance, and available resources.
Supply keyword exports, transcripts, survey responses, or competitor notes when evidence should guide priorities.
Review scores with sales, support, and subject matter experts before committing the editorial calendar.
anti_patterns: Do not choose topics only from search volume without product and customer relevance.
Do not create dedicated pillar URLs when standard blog organization and internal linking are sufficient.
Do not publish an unbalanced calendar that ignores decision and implementation content.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide business goals, audience details, product problems, customer questions, existing content, competitors, and available resources.

faq.question: Can this skill write complete articles?
faq.answer: No. It plans what to create and directs full article writing to a copywriting skill.

faq.question: Does it conduct keyword research?
faq.answer: It organizes supplied exports and suggests queries. Live metrics require provided data or external research tools.

faq.question: Can it improve an existing content library?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide content and performance data to identify clusters, gaps, and update priorities.

faq.question: Does it help with headless CMS planning?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers platform selection, content models, editorial workflows, SEO fields, permissions, and integration considerations.

faq.question: What does a completed strategy include?
faq.answer: It includes three to five pillars, priority topics, buyer stages, content types, rationale, and a topic-cluster map.
